profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Jacksonville) is located at 4905 Belfort Road, Suite 145, Jacksonville, FL 32256. The operator publishes a footprint of 35184 square feet and 1.39 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18. Duke Energy, a major Florida utility, announced a five-year, $103 billion growth plan in 2026 that it expects to grow further, targeting 20 gigawatts of new generation over the coming decade; the company said AI data center customers including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta were a primary driver alongside population growth of roughly 200,000 people a year into its service territory and grid-hardening investment against severe weather, per Fortune's reporting. Duke CEO Harry Sideris said hyperscale data center customers are paying for their own dedicated infrastructure and that broader rate increases stem mainly from population growth and grid resilience work rather than data centers alone; in Florida specifically, Duke has been replacing wooden utility poles with steel and concrete as part of its storm-hardening strategy. About 60% of Duke's planned capital spending is allocated to new generation (gas turbines, solar, battery storage, and nuclear plant life extensions) and the remaining 40% to grid expansion and upgrades. Duke separately confirmed in 2025 that it was exploring building data centers of its own in Florida, according to WUSF's reporting.

Florida's data center sales-tax landscape changed materially in 2025: House Bill 7031, effective August 1, 2025, eliminated the state's sales-tax exemption on equipment, electricity, and construction materials for data centers with IT loads below 100 megawatts, preserving the exemption only for facilities at or above that threshold, with no grandfather clause for existing sub-100 MW facilities, per Ryan LLC's tax-advisory analysis. All of Flexential's Florida buildings, including this one, operate well under that 100 MW threshold, meaning they and their colocation tenants would no longer qualify for the exemption on new purchases made after the effective date, a shift that has been reported to create potential retroactive tax exposure and pressure toward lease renegotiations for smaller colocation operators statewide.

reading.body:
Flexential Jacksonville publishes 1.39 MW of critical load UPS capacity, ranking fourth among Florida's four data centers with disclosed power figures and representing 15 percent of the state's total published capacity.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and ISO 27001, which qualify it for regulated workloads in finance and healthcare. These attestations do not indicate whether the site currently hosts AI tenants, GPU infrastructure, or accelerators. The certifications establish baseline compliance but reveal nothing about actual AI training or inference workload presence.

At 1.39 MW across 35,184 square feet, this facility operates at a scale far below the megawatt-plus thresholds now standard for AI-focused compute campuses. Florida has 13 mapped data center facilities overall, but only four publish power capacity at all. The absence of published cooling specifications, electrical redundancy architecture, or infrastructure detail designed for high-density GPU density means the site's actual constraint on AI workload is unknowable from available data.
